status_summary: New START and its central limits expired on 2026-02-05 without a formal U.S. response to Russia's offer to keep observing them for a year, per the Arms Control Association, and that day the President posted on Truth Social (read on an archived copy) that the United States should have its nuclear experts work on a new, improved and modernized treaty rather than extend New START, without mentioning China or missile defense. On 2026-02-06 Under Secretary of State Thomas DiNanno told the Conference on Disarmament that a bilateral treaty with Russia alone is inappropriate, that a new arrangement must account for all Russian nuclear weapons and China's buildup and meet U.S. verification standards, and that the United States may expand forces if the President directs. On 2026-02-17 Assistant Secretary of State Christopher Yeaw said at the Hudson Institute (transcript hosted by hudson.org) that the United States had proposed multilateral strategic stability talks and that the President wants China in a new agreement, though the path is likely difficult; the transcript does not mention missile defense. China has said it will not join nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage, Russia and China criticized the U.S. missile defense plan in a joint statement of 2026-05-20, and no official U.S. statement on keeping homeland missile defense out of negotiations was found.

timeline.event: The President posted on Truth Social at 1:47 PM Eastern, the day New START expired, that the United States should have its nuclear experts work on a new, improved and modernized treaty rather than extend New START; the post does not mention China or missile defense (read on a third-party archive).

Under Secretary of State Thomas DiNanno told the Conference on Disarmament that a new arrangement must account for all Russian nuclear weapons and China's stockpile growth, that a Russia-only treaty is inappropriate, and that U.S. forces could be expanded if the President directs; the remarks were circulated as document CD/2498.

At the Hudson Institute, Assistant Secretary of State Christopher Yeaw said the United States had proposed multilateral strategic stability talks, that the President wants China in a new agreement although the path is likely difficult, and that coming talks may address nuclear testing and verification; the transcript does not mention missile defense.

title: Orient arms control to U.S. interests and keep homeland missile defense off the table
uncertainties: The President's 2026-02-05 post was read on 2026-10-19 on a third-party archive (trumpstruth.org), by the researcher and confirmed by the reviewer,, because the original Truth Social address could not be retrieved; its New START passage was also seen in a newsletter and a news article carrying wire copy. The post is silent on China and missile defense. The Yeaw remarks of 2026-02-17 were read as a transcript on the Hudson Institute site, which is not an official State Department release; the transcript is silent on missile defense and Golden Dome. The 2026-02-06 remarks were read in the Conference on Disarmament document CD/2498 (issued 2026-02-11), which does not mention missile defense. Under the stage rubric, a posture statement is at most proposed, and absence of an agreement is not an action. The expiry without a formal U.S. response to Russia's offer rests on Arms Control Association summaries, an advocacy-leaning research group, which were not re-opened on 2026-10-19 and remain in the sources. The 2026-05-20 Russia and China statement was read through a Reuters item syndicated by TimesLIVE. The Mandate's missile defense exclusion was also listed as not verified in c04-07; no 2025 or 2026 official statement on excluding homeland defense from talks was found. Searches for talks after February 2026 were limited; later developments may have been missed. The agency field names the Department of State as the actor for these statements; the chapter is the Department of Defense chapter.
